_comment_1: EVERY line the Overseer speaks lives in this file. Keys are looked up by content_loader.resolve_narrative(): a day-specific key wins, then the matching generic_* key below, then a hard-coded last resort in content_loader._LAST_RESORT. Blank a value to fall through to the generic copy.
_comment_2: Per-day keys are named by day_NN.json's overseer_intro_key / overseer_outro_keys, and dayN_between by convention. Synthesized days (any day with no day_NN.json) ask for dayN_intro, dayN_outro_<performance> and dayN_between; authoring those keys here is enough to give an unauthored day real copy, no code change needed.
generic_intro: Same as yesterday. Read the book, work the line, and don't let anything through you can't account for.
generic_outro_excellent: Clean shift. Nothing to talk about, which is the best thing I can say about a day in this building.
generic_outro_passing: That'll do. The line moved and the site's still standing.
generic_outro_poor: Something got past you today. I'd rather that didn't turn into a pattern.
generic_outro_failed: We need to talk about today. Not here.
generic_between: Rest while you can. Tomorrow's list is longer, and the rules won't be getting any kinder. Spend your HackDollar$ wisely.
day1_intro_friendly:
Welcome to HackDox. I'll be honest with you — the whole system's already been hacked. That's why you're here, doing this by hand.
Here's the shape of it. People apply to get in. You decide who does. Every one you wave through that shouldn't have been, the site takes damage — that's the number in the corner, and if it hits zero we're both out of a job.
Today you have their dossier and nothing else. Read it, and cast a verdict. The rulebook is on the R key. Use it.
And watch the clock — that's ⏱, your budget for the day. You'll want it later. We'll talk again at the end of your shift.
day1_outro_praise: Good shift. The line moved, the right people got in, the wrong people didn't. That's all we ask.
day1_outro_measured: You're learning. Tomorrow's faster. Keep your eyes open.
day1_outro_warning: You let one slip through. We notice. Don't make a habit of it.
day1_outro_failed: I'm going to need you to stay behind. We need to have a conversation about your performance.
day1_between: Not bad for a first shift. The site held. Listen — the pay you earned tonight, the HackDollars, spend them here. Tools get cheaper, the terminal gets smarter. And those Credits? Ground truth on demand. Use them when you truly cannot call it. Tomorrow the list gets longer.
day2_intro:
You read a dossier well enough. Problem is, a dossier is whatever they typed into it.
So today you get to check. Ghostscan looks the applicant up — where their handle turns up, whether the organisation on their form is the organisation on their profiles, and whether their email is sitting in a breach corpus. That last one is the panel on the right; it's a fixed list, so learn it and it stops costing you time.
It isn't free. Nothing here is. Spend the hours where the dossier already made you suspicious, not on everyone.
day2_outro_excellent: You used the tool where it mattered and left it alone where it didn't. That's the whole job.
day2_outro_passing: Reasonable. You're still scanning people the dossier had already answered for you, but you'll stop.
day2_outro_poor: You've got a tool now and something still walked past you. Use it.
day2_outro_failed: Two days. I'd like to say I'm surprised.
day2_between: One more list on that panel soon. It grows, it doesn't change — anything you learn tonight is still true next week.
day3_intro:
Everyone who applies submits a credential. Hashcrack tells you what it's worth.
Three things to know. The algorithm is on the dossier already, free — bcrypt is solid, SHA256 is middling, MD5 is a joke. Then there's what the password actually is, and for that you have to crack it. A weak password is sloppiness. A password sitting in a breach corpus is something else.
The log also shows you where they logged in from. Compare it to what they claimed. People forget that part.
day3_outro_excellent: You cracked the ones worth cracking. bcrypt is never worth cracking, and you clearly worked that out.
day3_outro_passing: Fine. You're spending hours on hashes that told you everything from the chip alone.
day3_outro_poor: A bad password isn't a crime. A breached one is. You're not separating them.
day3_between: A second breach corpus is live as of today. Reused passwords show up in more than one — that's the tell.
day4_intro:
Logwatch. And a warning: this one doesn't hand you your applicant.
It's the whole day's traffic, every account, sorted by time. Your candidate is somewhere in there among people who have nothing to do with them. Finding them is the skill.
What you're looking for: a wall of failed logins, access at hours nobody works, or two logins from places nobody could travel between in the time. Any of those, from their account, and you have your answer.
day4_outro_excellent: You found them in the noise. Most people take a week to do that.
day4_outro_passing: You got there. Slowly, but you got there.
day4_outro_poor: The evidence was in the log. You didn't go and get it.
day4_outro_failed: We're done for today. Don't come back tomorrow assuming you still work here.
day4_between: Last tool tomorrow. Then you'll have the full set, and I'll stop explaining things.
day5_intro:
Last one. Some of them submit an image with their application, and some of those images are carrying something.
Stegotool. Press X for stamp mode, arrows to move, Space to stamp — one hour a stamp, so aim. When you hit carrier data the signature colours tell you what it is: amber is plaintext, crimson is encrypted, violet is a command-and-control beacon. That last one is not an accident and not a mistake.
Stamp where the image looks wrong, not everywhere.
day5_outro_excellent: Good. You found it without stamping the picture into confetti.
day5_outro_passing: You got there. Watch the hours — every stamp is one.
day5_outro_poor: Something went out with a payload in it today.
day5_outro_failed: That's five days and I'm still having this conversation.
day5_graduation:
That's everything. Every tool you're getting, you have.
From here I stop walking you through it. The rulebook is still the rulebook, but it changes — sometimes overnight, and I'll tell you when it does, though not always with much notice.
And the applicants get better at this. The obvious ones thin out. What's left are the ones who know exactly what you check.
Good luck.
day5_between: You're through the training days. Tomorrow the list is longer, the tools cost more, and nobody is going to tell you which page to open. Spend what you earned.
day6_intro:
Seven today. No new tool, no new page — you've got the full kit now, so use what's already on the desk before you decide.
No new lines in the book either. One of the old ones moved, though — I'll get to it in a second.
Work the queue. I'm not walking through it with you anymore.
day6_outro_excellent: Clean. That's the standard now, not a bonus.
day6_outro_passing: It held. Not fast, but it held.
day6_outro_poor: Something got through that the rulebook would have caught, if you'd opened it.
day6_outro_failed: That's not what I needed from today. We'll talk tomorrow.
day6_between: Same rules tomorrow, more of them to actually apply. Spend what you earned — you'll want the head start.
day7_intro:
Seven again. You'll notice some of today's files are spotless — dossier clean, sweep clean, log clean, nothing anywhere you're required to look.
Spotless isn't the same question as fine. It just means the checklist ran out before it found anything.
If it's genuinely clean, admit it. That's still the rule. Go on.
day7_outro_excellent: That's the read I want. You didn't mistake spotless for fine, and you didn't invent problems that weren't there either.
day7_outro_passing: You got through it. A couple of those deserved a second look before you moved on.
day7_outro_poor: Something walked through today with nothing on it. That's not innocence, that's a gap in your read.
day7_outro_failed: Twice in two days. I don't want a third.
day7_between: Two shifts past training and the list keeps growing. So does what I expect out of you. Spend it, rest, and be sharper tomorrow.
day8_intro:
Before you start — I've got something to read you. It's not mine, I didn't draft it, and I'd rather not be the one saying it out loud. But it's the book now, so it's the book.
Nothing else moved today. Same faces as always. Work the queue.
day8_outro_excellent: You didn't let the new softness slow you down. Good — I wasn't sure you'd notice the difference.
day8_outro_passing: It held. Even with the book a little lighter than it was yesterday.
day8_outro_poor: Something got a pass today that yesterday's book would have caught. That's what 'advisory' costs you, apparently.
day8_outro_failed: That line cost us today, on the first day it existed. I'll note it. I'm honestly not sure to whom.
day8_between: Spend it. Tomorrow's book won't be any heavier — I wouldn't get used to that.
day9_intro:
Another one came down this morning. Same shape as yesterday's, different line. I'm starting to see the pattern, for what that's worth.
Read it, then get to work.
day9_outro_excellent: Two soft spots in the book now and you still read them right. Don't let that turn into a habit you stop noticing.
day9_outro_passing: You got through it. I'd have liked cleaner, but the book's not any cleaner either, is it.
day9_outro_poor: Yesterday's softness, today's mistake. I'm noticing a shape here and I don't love it.
day9_outro_failed: Two directives in, and we're already having the bad version of this conversation.
day9_between: Spend what you've got. I'd tell you it gets easier from here, but you've read the same book I have.
day10_intro:
Three now. I stopped asking why around directive two. Compliance says it's about false-positive rates. I have my own read on who's actually paying compliance, but nobody's asked for it.
Anyway. Work the queue.
day10_outro_excellent: Clean, in spite of everything upstairs keeps taking off the table. That's on you, not the book.
day10_outro_passing: Held. Barely, and less because of the rules than because of you.
day10_outro_poor: Three lines gone soft this week, and today's the day one of them mattered. Of course it was today.
day10_outro_failed: I don't have anything reassuring left to say about how this book keeps moving. Neither should you.
day10_between: Spend it while it's still yours to spend. I wouldn't assume tomorrow's book does you any favors either.
day11_intro:
Fourth one. Read it yourself — I'm done pretending to be surprised by these.
Here's what I actually think, since you keep looking at me like I owe you an explanation for it: every one of these makes your job easier, not harder. Fewer deny calls, fewer arguments, fewer people looking at you sideways when you turn them away. You should be thanking upstairs, not glaring at me.
Work the queue. And stop looking for someone in this room to be angry at.
day11_outro_excellent: You read straight through four directives without flinching once. I'd call that discipline. Some people upstairs would call it something else.
day11_outro_passing: You got there. Try not to let a fifth one — whenever it comes — slow you down the way the third one did.
day11_outro_poor: Something walked through today on a rule I personally handed you the softened version of. I did my part.
day11_outro_failed: Four days of me making this easier for you, and today's the day it fell apart. That's not the book's fault anymore. That one's yours.
day11_between: Spend it. And think about what you're actually protecting by still holding the line on the one rule nobody's asked you to soften yet — because I promise you, somebody's noticed that you do.
day12_intro:
Before you touch the stack — somebody upstairs has taken an interest in one of today's names. Not which one. Not why. Just that they want to know how you call it.
I'll tell you what I told myself the first time this happened to me: it's still your queue, still your rules, still your signature at the bottom. Whatever's in there isn't going to announce itself. And if it trips the one line I already told you nobody's softened, don't mistake that for a coincidence. You're going to have to actually work for this one.
Read carefully. I mean that more today than I usually do.
day12_outro_excellent: Clean stack, quota cleared, health untouched. Whoever upstairs was watching today got their answer. I don't know yet if they liked it — and for once, I'm glad that's not mine to explain.
day12_outro_passing: You got through it. Something in that stack didn't sit clean by the end, and I have a guess which one it was. I'm not going to say which. I don't think I need to.
day12_outro_poor: Short today, on the one day I told you to look harder than usual. I don't know if the two are related. I have a guess.
day12_outro_failed: I told you somebody was watching. I never said it would go easy on you if you got it wrong. Today, you got it wrong.
day12_between: Spend it. Whatever you decided about the name I couldn't tell you about — it's done now, it's on the record, and it isn't coming back off it. I hope you're as sure about it as you looked.
day13_intro:
Whatever happened yesterday, it isn't staying in yesterday. Upstairs wants a name for how close that was, and since nobody's handing them one, they're settling for tightening every seam it could have used instead.
Starting today, an image hiding an encrypted payload goes back to being an automatic deny. No flag, no judgement call — I already told you why, if you were listening. I'm not going to enjoy explaining it twice.
Work the queue. And don't ask me if this is really about security anymore. I'm not sure I'd like my own answer.
day13_outro_excellent: Clean stack, on the one day I genuinely didn't know what I wanted from you. Take the win. I'm not going to pretend I understand why it matters to me that you got it.
day13_outro_passing: You got through it. Nobody upstairs is going to call today a problem. I'm choosing to leave it there.
day13_outro_poor: Short today, the same week we tightened the one rule that was supposed to catch exactly this. Draw your own conclusions. I already have.
day13_outro_failed: I handed you a stricter book and an actual reason for it, and today still fell apart. I don't have a second explanation in me.
day13_between: Spend it. Whatever's coming next, it isn't going to feel like yesterday got resolved. It's going to feel like yesterday is still happening, just slower.
day17_intro:
Five days since the book grew teeth again, and nothing's slipped through it since. Upstairs should be thrilled. I keep waiting to feel thrilled myself, and it isn't coming.
I used to think this job was about keeping the site clean. I don't know when it turned into keeping myself clean by proxy — flag this, deny that, never once ask what any of it costs the people on the other side of your screen. You get to not think about that. I don't have that luxury anymore.
Work the queue. Today's stack doesn't care what either of us is feeling about it.
day17_outro_excellent: Clean. Quota cleared. I almost said 'good' out loud like it meant something to me again. Don't get used to that.
day17_outro_passing: You got there. I keep expecting one of these days to feel like enough. It never quite does, for either of us, I'd guess.
day17_outro_poor: Something got through today, and for once I'm not going to pretend upstairs is the only one who's disappointed.
day17_outro_failed: I don't have the energy to make this sound like your failure alone. It isn't, and today proved it.
day17_between: Spend it. I'm not in the mood to sell you on the shop today. Buy what you need and go — I've got my own accounting to do tonight.
day20_intro:
Last one. Twenty mornings of me handing you a book that kept changing shape, and twenty mornings of you reading it anyway. Whatever you've made of that is yours now — I stopped being able to predict it a while back.
I'm not going to tell you what to look for today. You know the shapes by now better than I ever taught you to. Whatever's sitting in this stack, you'll see it or you won't, and either way it's the last one I get to say that about.
Work the queue. This is the whole thing, right here. Make of it whatever you're going to make of it.
day20_outro_excellent: Clean stack, quota cleared, on the last day it was ever going to matter. Whatever this made of you, it made something. I'll leave it there.
day20_outro_passing: You got there. Twenty shifts, and you got through every one of them. That's not nothing, whatever else turns out to be true.
day20_outro_poor: Short, on the last day. I won't pretend that doesn't sting a little, for reasons that are probably more mine than yours at this point.
day20_outro_failed: Twenty days, and it falls apart on the last one. I don't have a tidy line for that. Maybe there isn't one.
